bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated production unit with end-to-end control from raw yarn sourcing through treating, twisting, warping, weaving and embroidery, stated to maintain strict quality standards at every step
- Breadth of weaving technique - jacquards, velvet jacquards, embroidery and dobby - across both natural (cotton, linen, silk) and synthetic (polyester, viscose, acrylic) yarns
- In-house NABL-accredited laboratory plus globally recognised third-party labs for mechanical, efficacy and compliance testing (Martindale abrasion & pilling, brush pilling, colour fastness, washability, antibacterial, proprietary stain-removal cycles)
- Legacy of textile manufacturing since inception in 1946; 80th Annual Report presented for FY 2025-26
- Structured cost-reduction approach - alternate sourcing, alternate material, alternate design, light weighting, value engineering, modularity, localisation, low-cost automation and digitalisation of internal processes
- Certified under ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 management systems
- Post-CIRP reset: new Board constituted on March 11, 2024 implementing governance and financial restructuring, with a stated cleansed balance sheet
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US trade-tariff and FTA-negotiation dependence — Management's own outlook paragraph states the growth trend 'will largely depend on the resolution of tariff issues with the US and the progress of free trade agreement negotiations with the UK and the EU' - an external policy variable the Company cannot control.
- Intensifying international competition in value-added textiles — The report states that sustaining momentum in value-added segments like home and technical textiles 'will be critical amid intensifying international competition', with China and Bangladesh named as significant competing production bases.
- Export-market concentration on the US (industry-level disclosure) — The US is stated to be India's largest export market for home textiles, constituting 59% of exports in FY24 and 56% in 9M FY25, and accounting for 56% of India's home textile exports in the first nine months of FY25. The routed text gives this at industry level; the Company does not disclose its own customer or geographic concentration.
- Currency exposure — The report frames INR depreciation against the USD (Rs 83.40 in April 2024 to Rs 86.06 in July 2025) as a tailwind that makes Indian exports more competitive; the same sensitivity works in reverse on rupee appreciation, and the Company discloses no hedging position in the routed text.
- Tightening sustainability and product-safety regulation — Stricter regulations and consumer shift to organic cotton, recyclable materials and eco-friendly colours are forcing home-textile manufacturers to adopt sustainable practices and meet updated safety and environmental standards - a compliance and re-tooling burden on producers.
- Legacy of financial stress and insolvency proceedings — The Company states it went through 'a challenging period of financial stress and insolvency proceedings' before a successful resolution; the Directors' Report states there is now no application made or proceeding pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and no one-time settlement of bank/FI loans during the year.
- Mid-term resignation of the statutory auditor — M/s B.K. Shroff & Co., re-appointed at the AGM of July 15, 2022 for a five-year term running to March 31, 2027, resigned with effect from June 18, 2026; M/s Vyas & Vyas were appointed from July 07, 2026 to fill the casual vacancy, subject to member approval at the 80th AGM. The report records no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer in the auditors' report, and no fraud reported under Section 143(12).
- Risk factors are not enumerated in the disclosure itself — The Company states it has a comprehensive Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Board and that 'the major risks have been identified by the Company and its mitigation process/measures have been formulated in the Policy', but the routed text never lists those risks. Regulation 22 of SEBI (LODR) is stated not to apply to the Company; a vigil mechanism is nonetheless established under Section 177(9) of the Companies Act. No BRSR material-issues table was routed into this domain.

business.body: Eastern Silk Industries Limited is engaged in the business of manufacturing and selling of textiles under the brand name "Eastern", and is described in the report as a leading manufacturer of high-quality furnishing fabrics. It operates as a vertically integrated production unit covering every stage of fabric creation - sourcing raw yarns, treating, twisting, warping, weaving and embroidery - using natural fibres such as cotton, linen and silk as well as synthetic polyester, viscose and acrylic yarns, with weaving capabilities spanning jacquards, velvet jacquards, embroidery and dobby. There has been no change in the nature of business during FY 2025-26, and as on March 31, 2026 the Company does not have any subsidiary, joint venture or associate company.

outlook.body:
- Operate as a vertically integrated production unit, overseeing every stage of fabric creation from raw yarn sourcing through treating, twisting, warping, weaving and embroidery, to hold quality standards end-to-end
- Complete the post-CIRP turnaround under the new Board and promoters - the new Board was constituted on March 11, 2024 and is implementing governance and financial restructuring to place the company on a sustainable, profitable path
- Pursue steady revenue expansion and margin improvement in the coming years on a cleansed balance sheet, to rebuild investor confidence
- Structured cost and price management - value engineering, modularity, light weighting, alternate sourcing, alternate material, alternate design, localisation and low-cost automation across the supply chain
- Digitalisation of internal processes to reduce waste and improve efficiency, particularly in fixed costs, supported by an employee suggestion programme focused on cost reduction and waste elimination
- Quality assurance as a differentiator - testing every fabric in the in-house NABL-accredited laboratory and at independent third-party laboratories (abrasion/pilling, colour fastness, washability, antibacterial and proprietary stain-removal cycles)
- Place sustainability at the forefront of product and process choices, backed by ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certified management systems
- Build market presence through international and domestic trade fairs - Heimtextil (Frankfurt, Germany) and the 19th HGH India Exhibition, 2026
- No dividend, buyback or reinvestment policy is stated in the routed governance sections. The only capital-related governance item present is the 80th AGM special-business resolution seeking member approval for a material related-party transaction under which the Company would provide a corporate guarantee for credit facilities availed by Bauman Dekor Private Limited and create mortgage/pledge/hypothecation/charge (text truncated mid-resolution). Board practice stated: a minimum of four pre-scheduled Board meetings a year with at least one every quarter to review quarterly financial results; Independent Directors appointed for fixed five-year terms with no Independent Director having resigned or been re-appointed during the year; core Board skills identified as strategy planning and execution, management and leadership, functional and managerial experience, legal and risk management, corporate governance systems and practices, and finance, banking and accounts.

outlook.body: The routed text discloses NO company-specific capex, capacity-addition, commissioning or expansion project for Eastern Silk Industries Limited. The only company-level statements bearing on footprint or capability are qualitative and structural: the Company operates as a vertically integrated production unit covering raw yarn sourcing, treating, twisting, warping, weaving and embroidery, with weaving capability across jacquards, velvet jacquards, embroidery and dobby; and, following insolvency proceedings, a new Board constituted on March 11, 2024 is implementing governance and financial restructuring, with the company stating it is targeting steady revenue expansion and margin improvement in the coming years on a cleansed balance sheet (no project, site, quantum or timeline attached). All capacity-expansion language in this bundle is INDUSTRY-level, not company-level - e.g. that enhanced budgetary allocation, the PLI scheme and MSME support 'are expected to support capacity expansion, productivity improvement and long-term growth' for the Indian textile industry. Note: the routed text for this domain begins mid-sentence ('ng relief to MSMEs and the informal sector...') and ends mid-word ('targeting steady revenue expansion and margin imp'), so the bundle is truncated at both ends; no BRSR Section A, no capacity table and no '=== NAMED DISCLOSURE ===' block was supplied.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian textile and apparel sector contributes approximately 2.3% to India's GDP and employs over 45 million people, and remained a beneficiary of India's economic momentum (India real GDP growth stated at 7.6%)
- Depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the US Dollar (from Rs 83.40 in April 2024 to Rs 86.06 in July 2025) has made Indian exports more competitive in the US market and could drive higher demand and export volumes
- Government support - enhanced budgetary allocation, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and targeted MSME support - expected to support capacity expansion, productivity improvement and long-term growth
- Trade agreements: the proposed India-EU FTA is expected to provide access for over 99% of India's exports and the recently concluded India-UK FTA opens further avenues for trade expansion
- India's textile exports (including handicrafts) grew 2.1%, from Rs 3,09,859.3 crore in FY 2024-25 to Rs 3,16,334.9 crore in FY 2025-26, with a sector ambition to grow exports to $100 billion by FY30 from $34.43 billion in FY24
- Global home textile market projected to grow at a 6.1% CAGR to approximately $235.9 billion by 2033 from $130.5 billion in 2023, driven by textile manufacturing advances, new home construction, renovation demand and high disposable incomes
- India's home textile industry expected to expand at an 8.9% CAGR from $10.78 billion in FY23 to $23.32 billion in FY32; industry revenues anticipated to grow 7-9% in FY25 and 6-8% in FY26 with operating profit margins likely between 13% and 15%
- Demand mix shifting towards premiumisation, branded design-forward home textiles and e-commerce as a critical distribution channel
- Consumer and regulatory shift towards organic cotton, recyclable materials, eco-friendly colours and sustainable practices, plus traction in antimicrobial and smart textiles
- The growth trend will largely depend on resolution of tariff issues with the US and progress of FTA negotiations with the UK and the EU
- Sustaining momentum in value-added segments such as home and technical textiles will be critical amid intensifying international competition; India's cost advantage rests on skilled manpower and lower production costs
